question.text: If a bond has POSITIVE convexity, which of the following is true?

answer.text: Price rises LESS than duration predicts when yields fall
Price rises MORE than duration predicts when yields fall, AND falls LESS when yields rise
Price is invariant to yield changes

explanation.text: The Logic: Positive convexity is the asymmetric benefit: duration-only estimates underestimate upside and overestimate downside. Net: expected return > same-duration, lower-convexity bond. The Trap: Convexity is a second-order effect; it adjusts duration estimates for large rate moves. Cross-Exam Context: IV covers convexity math; XXI-B emphasises portfolio construction implication. Manager's Pro-Tip: Paying up for convexity (e.g., via long-duration zero-coupons) is worth it when rate volatility is expected — it's a volatility trade in disguise.
